newsitem.title: USA: Last round of meat talks productive - US official.
newsitem.headline: Last round of meat talks productive - US official.

text.p: The senior U.S. negotiator in talks with the European Union to settle a dispute over meat imports said Thursday that this week's meetings have been "productive" even if they haven't resulted in an agreement.
"We went through the remaining issues at some length ... we had, I think a productive meeting," said Paul Drazek, senior trade adviser to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.
"There's been no agreement, but we've continuing to talk," he said after the officials met Tuesday and Wednesday in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks.

Negotiators were scheduled to meet briefly Thursday morning, and the EU team was then departing for Brussels in the afternoon. There was talk that the meetings would be continued next week in Brussels.

EU and U.S. officials have been trying to reach agreement over differences in their meat import inspection regulations. A deal would enable the two sides to accept meat and poultry from each other even if the inspection systems differ.
Failure to reach agreement could disrupt the trans-Atlantic flow of trade of hundreds of millions of dollars worth of poultry and meat products.
